decisions.reason: A complete same-message MODIFY already records that the approved Hero V is the fixed reference and that the É accent must adapt to it while preserving the shared peak horizon.
A complete same-message MODIFY already records that the E and L forms, as surrounding type, must adapt to the approved Hero V rather than requiring changes to it.
The candidate already requires literal derivation from the approved Hero V terminal with an exact vector match; restoring that approved Hero V does not change this requirement.
The candidate already defines the shared terminal gesture by reference to the approved Hero V and remains valid unchanged when that geometry is restored.
The second V is already required to derive its geometry and signature gesture from the approved Option 2 Hero V; the source restores that reference without introducing a new second-V rule.
Restoring the Hero V geometry does not alter the second V's established relative height or subordinate visual role.
The source changes the fixed geometric reference for adapting the type, but it does not change the requirement that kerning make the wordmark read as one unified mark.
The source concerns geometric restoration and type adaptation, not the deferred champagne material treatment or its role.
The Hero V restoration decision does not change the task-local obligation to include design rationale with review rounds.
